title: Replacing a local surface resolution by normalized point blowups
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian normal local domain of Krull dimension $2$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Assume there is an integral regular scheme $T$ and a proper morphism $T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ inducing an isomorphism of function fields [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sc-function-field]. Then there is a finite sequence $X_n\to\cdots\to X_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of proper morphisms, with $X_n$ regular, in which every $X_{j+1}\to X_j$ is the composite of the blowup of $X_j$ at a closed point (with its reduced closed subscheme structure) and the normalization of that blowup in its function field [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-sc-normalization]. All these schemes are integral and normal, all normalizations used are finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and all centers lie above the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. The sequence may have length zero.

proof.text: Apply the regular-model completion lemma to the given $T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. It supplies a complete Noetherian normal local domain $C=\widehat A$ and an integral regular proper birational model $T_C\to\operatorname{Spec}C$. The completion-dimension theorem gives $\dim C=\dim A=2$. It is enough to construct a proper normalized point-blowup tower with regular endpoint over $C$: the existing completion-descent theorem will then give the required tower over $A$, including regularity of its endpoint. We construct that tower in Steps 2--7 rather than assuming that domination alone preserves regularity.

source.place: Tag 0BGM, first paragraph; Tags 0BGI and 0BG6. Descent is applied explicitly in Step 8.

proof.text: The complete-local excellence theorem makes $C$ excellent. The finite-type Noetherian theorem and excellent finite-type/localization stability make $T_C$ Noetherian and excellent. The closed-dominant dimension theorem applies to its proper birational map to $\operatorname{Spec}C$: the function-field extension has transcendence degree zero, so $\dim T_C=2$. Apply normalized domination to this map, obtaining $Y=Y_n\to\cdots\to Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and a factorization $q:Y\to T_C$. Apply the excellent normalized-tower geometry theorem: since the normal base has trivial initial normalization, every $Y_j$ is integral, normal, excellent, Noetherian and two-dimensional, and every normalization used is finite. All arrows are proper by the domination theorem. The composite $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ of these proper arrows is proper by composition of proper morphisms, so the factor $q$ is proper by proper-to-separated cancellation over $\operatorname{Spec}C$, and is birational because both structure maps identify their function fields with $\operatorname{Frac}C$.

source.place: Tag 0BGM, second and third paragraphs; Tag 0BBT. The dimension and properness checks are expanded.

proof.text: Apply the excellent-normal-surface local-data theorem to $Y$. Its singular set is a finite set of closed points $y_1,\ldots,y_t$, and $B_a=\mathcal O_{Y,y_a}$ is an excellent Noetherian normal local domain of dimension $2$. Each $B_a$ is a localization of a finite-type $C$-algebra: choose an affine neighbourhood of $y_a$ in the finite-type $C$-scheme $Y$ and localize at its prime. If $t=0$, $Y$ is already regular and the subsequent local choices are empty.

source.place: Tag 0BGM, third paragraph, the finitely many singular points of the normal dominating model.

proof.text: Fix $a$, put $x_a=q(y_a)$ and $R_a=\mathcal O_{T_C,x_a}$. The regular scheme $T_C$ is normal by regular-implies-normal. At a codimension-one point its one-dimensional Noetherian normal local domain is a DVR. Thus the modification-codimension-one theorem applied to $q$ gives an isomorphism over every point of codimension zero or one in $T_C$. If $x_a$ had either codimension, the local ring at $y_a$ would be a regular local ring of $T_C$, a contradiction. Since $\dim T_C=2$, $R_a$ has dimension $2$. It is regular, and is excellent by finite-type/localization stability over $C$. The local map $R_a\hookrightarrow B_a$ is injective and identifies their fraction fields by birationality. It is essentially of finite type: in affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ for $q$, $E$ is finite type over $D$; if the primes are $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$, then $E_{\mathfrak q}$ is the localization of $E\otimes_DD_{\mathfrak p}$ at the induced prime. Apply the birational-local rationality lemma to $R_a\subset B_a$. It gives $H^1(Z,\mathcal O_Z)=0$ for every normal proper birational model of $\operatorname{Spec}B_a$.

source.place: Tag 0BGM, paragraph Let x_a; Tags 0B4Q and 0BG0. The local-extension hypotheses and the dimension of R_a are checked explicitly.

proof.text: For each $a$, apply the rational-surface point-blowup resolution lemma to $B_a$ over the complete local ring $C$. Step 3 supplied its essentially-finite-type presentation and dimension, and Step 4 supplied exactly its vanishing hypothesis. This gives an ordinary point-blowup tower $V_{a,m_a}\to\cdots\to V_{a,0}=\operatorname{Spec}B_a$ with integral normal intermediate schemes, proper arrows, centers over its closed point, and regular endpoint. Regard it as a normalized point-blowup tower: each ordinary blowup in this particular tower is already normal, so its normalization in its function field is the identity. Indeed on a normal affine chart the ring is integrally closed in its fraction field, which makes the integral closure used to define normalization equal to the ring itself. This changes neither the schemes nor the arrows.

source.place: Tag 0BGM, final two paragraphs: rational-to-Gorenstein followed by rational-double-point resolution. Normal intermediates permit normalized blowups without a further operation.

proof.text: Globalize these $t$ local proper normalized towers at the distinct closed points $y_a$ by the local-normalized-blowups globalization theorem. It gives a proper normalized point-blowup tower $W\to\cdots\to Y$, an isomorphism over the regular open $Y\setminus\{y_a\}$, and endpoint local-ring identifications over each $y_a$ with the local rings of $V_{a,m_a}$. Therefore $W$ is regular: a point over the regular open has its regular local ring unchanged, and a point over $y_a$ has the regular local ring of its corresponding point on $V_{a,m_a}$. These cases cover every point. In case $t=0$ this is the identity tower. Applying the excellent normalized-tower geometry theorem over $Y$ also shows that the intermediate schemes are integral, normal, excellent and Noetherian, and all their normalization morphisms are finite.

source.place: Tag 0BGM, final two paragraphs; globalization of the local modifications and the local-ring regularity check.

proof.text: Concatenate the first tower ending at $Y$ and the tower of Step 6. Its endpoint is regular. Every intermediate scheme is proper over $\operatorname{Spec}C$, by composition of proper morphisms. If $z$ is one of the chosen closed centers, its singleton is closed in that intermediate scheme; the proper structure map is closed, so its image is a closed singleton in $\operatorname{Spec}C$. Since $C$ is local, this image is its unique closed point. Hence all centers of the concatenated tower lie over that point, as required for completion descent.

source.place: Conclusion of the complete case in Tag 0BGM; the support of the centers follows from properness over a local base.

proof.text: Apply the normalized-blowup completion-descent theorem to $A\to C$. Step 1 supplied normality of the completion, and Steps 2--7 supplied a finite proper normalized point-blowup tower over $C$, supported over its closed point and with regular endpoint. Descent yields $X_N\to\cdots\to X_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with the same properties of properness and support of centers, and with $X_N$ regular. The theorem identifies the base change of the whole tower, including all structure maps. It explicitly allows length zero.

source.place: Tag 0BGM, first paragraph, applied after completing the complete case; Tags 0BGA and 0BG6(3).

proof.text: We check the remaining integral/normal clauses on the descended tower. Start with the normal integral base $\operatorname{Spec}A$. For an integral intermediate scheme, the ordinary point blowup is integral: on a nonempty affine open with domain $D$ and ideal $I$, its chart rings $D[I/a]\subset D_a\subset\operatorname{Frac}D$ are domains for nonzero generators $a$, and all these charts share the unchanged generic point. The zero-generator charts are empty; the point ideal is nonzero, since the intermediate scheme has dimension $2$ and its closed center cannot be its generic point. The chart-cover theorem covers the blowup by exactly these charts. Its normalization in the common function field is the relative normalization in $\operatorname{Spec}K$: the affine integral-closure description agrees with the definition of $(-)^\nu$. The relative-normalization theorem makes it integral, and the normalization-normal-stalks theorem makes all its local rings normal (the source $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is normal). The generic-point morphism to a Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so both theorems apply. Induction proves that all $X_j$ are integral and normal: after each normalization its proper birational map to the base has dimension $2$ by the closed-dominant dimension theorem, providing the dimension hypothesis for the next point blowup. Noetherianity at each stage follows from proper finite type over the Noetherian base.

source.place: Tag 0BBS and the normalization clauses following the definition of resolution by normalized blowups; divisors.tex Tag 02ND and morphisms.tex Tag 035Q. The required chart argument is written out.

proof.text:
For each descended arrow write $X_{j+1}\xrightarrow{
u_j}B_j=\operatorname{Bl}_{x_j}X_j	o X_j$. The normalization map is integral by the relative-normalization theorem, with the identification in Step 9. The blowup is proper by the blowup-proper theorem, since a reduced closed-point ideal on a Noetherian scheme is finite type and quasi-coherent, and in particular it is separated. The composite $X_{j+1}	o X_j$ is proper by Step 8. Apply proper-to-separated cancellation to this triangle to conclude that $
u_j$ is proper and therefore locally of finite type. The finite-iff-integral-and-locally-finite-type theorem now shows that $
u_j$ is finite. This proves the finiteness of every normalization without assuming that $A$ itself is excellent or Nagata. Together with Steps 8 and 9 it proves every clause of the statement.
